analysis.summary_md:
Measured today and with the design (massing.geojson in place of what it covers, same method): uses, edges, green (27.2 % without farmland, 30.7 ha open green, 52.9 m2 public green per resident at 5,000), walking reach (400 m: green 65 to 99 %, shops 12 to 98 %, schools 1 to 31 %), sealed share and keep; maps `*_design.png`, `comparison.csv` and `comparison.md` (11 better, 9 worse).
Sealed share: today 14.2 % fully, 8.3 % partly, 77.5 % unsealed; design 39.7 % fully (44.7 ha), 16.9 % partly (19.1 ha), 43.4 % unsealed (49.0 ha); farmland falls from 70.2 to 11.6 ha, and 0.2 ha is built over kept land.
Unsure of: wooded green reads 0.0 ha in the design (woods are probably covered by the design's open-space polygons, so check it); stations and bus stops are not in the data, so their reach is missing; retention basin, underpasses and 150 kV line are not in keep.geojson; sealing classes are assumptions; `measure.py` failed on a geometry overlay (grass polygon), so a patched copy with a 1 cm retry is in analysis/scripts/ (the skill's own file is unchanged and needs the same fix).

Rerun (art-direction fixes, drawings only; every number in comparison.csv is unchanged): (1) new ring charts `charts-sealing.png` (sealed share today 22.5 % and design 56.6 %, fully/partly/unsealed in % and ha) and `charts-green-per-resident.png` (52.9 m2 per resident with the design against the brief's 12 m2 minimum, p. 30; today has no per-resident figure, so none is drawn), made by `scripts/charts.py` from comparison.csv. (2) The walking-reach maps are now bands 0-200, 200-400 and 400-800 m in three tones with the buildings drawn over (200 m band is for the drawing only: `measure.py` copy adds it without a metrics row). Reach to green with the design is almost all within 200 m, so that map is mostly one tone, which is the finding.
analysis.unsure: of: wooded green reads 0.0 ha in the design (woods are probably covered by the design's open-space polygons, so check it); stations and bus stops are not in the data, so their reach is missing; retention basin, underpasses and 150 kV line are not in keep.geojson; sealing classes are assumptions; `measure.py` failed on a geometry overlay (grass polygon), so a patched copy with a 1 cm retry is in analysis/scripts/ (the skill's own file is unchanged and needs the same fix).
fixes: Add pie or ring charts for the sealed share today and with the design and for green per resident, with their numbers from comparison.csv, as the reference sums up the area figures in charts.
Draw the walking-reach maps as bands (0-200, 200-400 m) over the buildings rather than one solid dark-green area that covers the site; reach-green_design shows nothing but a filled shape.

climate.summary_md:

Key number: 21 % of the site is at 65 dB(A) or more by day (no homes; 16.7 % at the low traffic end, 22.2 % at the high end) and another 60 % at 55 to 65 (homes only behind a shielding edge); the cold-air corridor along Pilsen-Allee takes 4 % (3.5 to 5 %).
Least sure: noise, as the brief (p. 24) gives only 10,000 to 20,000 vehicles, so speeds (70, 100 km/h) are ASSUMED; the railway uses 2020 train counts (Bundestag 19/24091 p. 16) with ASSUMED lengths, brakes and speeds; DIN 18005 limits and RLS-90 are German defaults; the climate map has no legend and fits the streets to about 70 m.

massing.summary_md:
Placed 237 new buildings on the 13 north-south rows of the structure plan (mostly paired 12 m bars around 8 m garden lanes, with ensembles, L, U and town houses; halls and L's in the two workshop areas; U and L screens on the Railway and Pilsen rows), 2 nine-floor landmarks at the station, 209 kept buildings, the school, the pool, 3 daycares, the bus station, the market hall and 3 garages on the three centres, streets, squares, gardens and 999 street trees. The scripts are unchanged; config.json takes run-13's figure, with a new entry for the Woods edge row.
Gross floor area 572,700 m2, a floor area ratio of 0.51 on the 112.8 ha site and 1.37 on the 41.8 ha of new land. That is 3,279 homes at 95 m2 each, against the structure plan's 3,280 (brief 2,800 to 3,400, p. 30), and 236,200 m2 of commerce against 230,000 (276,000 at most). 29 floors came off to stay under the homes figure, 78 of 190 home buildings are at the 6-floor cap, 16 need better acoustic protection (65 dB(A) or more by day), and the public green is 32.5 ha against 7.3 ha.
Unsure of: no room was found on the Headland school centre for the school's 3,000 m2 sports field (p. 30). The pool has 2,700 of 3,000 m2 and the market hall 1,260 of 1,800 m2. The 95 m2 per home, the garage and bus hall sizes and the 9-floor landmarks are my assumptions. The script counts 6 secondary dead ends but doesn't say where they are. The 150 kV line, the canal and the basin come only from the structure plan's traced greens. The check plans use the fallback look, because draw.py doesn't read drawing-graphics/standard.md, and their 8 px legend is fine for a check but not for a panel. Compared with the winners' site plan, the biggest differences are: no green ground or tree canopy, buildings toned grey by height instead of white with roman storey numbers, and an even grain of bars instead of varied courtyard blocks.

narrative.summary_md:
Field Lines, "A district grown in the furrows of the field": the district is built in north-south strips that follow the grain of the field and the cold air, with open field strips kept between them and a car-free headland at the Wutzlhofen stop. The text for the jury, on the brief's eight points (p. 34) and closing with a list of where it falls short, is in narrative/text.md, and the 800-sign communication text (782 signs, p. 12) in narrative/communication.txt. narrative.md is unchanged.
Number that matters most: 17.1 ha of field strips stay open ground (structure-plan/checks.txt). Even so, 39.7 % of the site ends up fully sealed, against 14.2 % today and our own target of 35 % (analysis/comparison.csv). The gaps from the framework: 13 built strips lie between only 7 field strips, so not every second strip stays field; there are 3 garages instead of one at each strip head; no field strip follows the canal.
Least sure of: the shortfalls named in text.md. Phase 1 has 965 homes, 135 under 1,100; there is no room for the school's sports field and the schoolyard is 1,750 of 2,000 m²; the food market has 980 of 1,200 m², the pool 2,700 of 3,000 m² and retention 8,227 of 8,357 m³. Play is 8,087 m², short of the 8,804 m² needed for 5,869 residents; daycare 2 has 550 of 950 m² of play; 16 buildings stand at 65 dB(A) or more. The study site, the housing mix, construction methods and energy are only partly answered or open, and interim farming is proposed but not mapped. The sealing figure differs between analysis (39.7 %) and open-space (42.7 %), and the text uses analysis.

perspective.summary_md:
Two eye-level views at 1.65 m, rerun for art-direction's three fixes, rendered with Gemini (no style references sent): view-1 (edge: the lawn strip in front, new housing 20 m or more behind it, chosen again from the 3,160 of 6,387 candidates that pass the new tests) and view-2 (the square and street axis to the trees, same camera as before); 2 views as the brief asks (at least two, p. 34). Fixes made: (1) view-1 no longer has a wall: nearest facade 48 m away, under 40 % of the frame within 15 m (checked in code, 0 %); (2) the render prompt now forbids lettering, signs and unit numbers and orders the facade colours of the base, and the new walls came back white and pale grey with no "UNIT"/"KAFE"/"STUDIO" text; (3) each base now has 20 people and 3 bikes across fore- and middle ground and one tree crown cut by the frame edge (scripts changed in perspective/local/, copies of the skill's: draw_view.py figures and crown, render.py prompt closing, pick.py for the viewpoint test).

structure-plan.summary_md:
Figure: 13 north-south built strips (46.0 ha with centres) lie between 7 field strips: 35 m wide in the west, 45 m in the east, plus the cold-air field along Pilsen-Allee. The field strips cover 17.1 ha and all public green 30.7 ha, with a power-line meadow besides. The Headland is a 25 m car-free cross strip with a walk along the edge of the garden city. It carries the main centre (Headland station square, at the stop and the underpass) and the Headland school past the underpass; Chamer crossing is the local centre. Phase 1 (between Chamer Straße and the rail) holds 1,300 homes for 1,100 asked and 138,500 of 165,192 m² floor area. Phase 2 (east) holds 1,280 for 1,100 and 241,600 of 293,096 m². Phase 3 (west) holds 700 for 600 and 161,500 of 244,917 m². In all 3,280 homes (brief 2,800 to 3,400) and 230,000 of 230,000 m² commerce. `checks.txt` shows no SHORT, but it took six builds, not the four the skill allows. The site measures 112.8 ha; the brief says about 107 ha.
59 % of homes are within a 400 m walk of the stop (1,938 of 3,280, `checks.txt`): the phase 1 rows 46 to 100 %, the east rows 0 to 100 %, and the west rows beyond Chamer Straße 0 %.
Key hypothesis: phase 1 fits its homes only at 28 % ground cover, above the 22 % default, read from "Urbanes Gebiet, hohe Dichte" on the framework plan (p. 37). It also has only 27 % of the land for 32 to 39 % of the homes. A massing test of the four phase 1 rows would settle it. The stop, the 150 kV line and the compensation land are read off the p. 37 plans, accurate to about 40 m (georef.py would settle them). No layer shows the main collector canal, so no field strip follows it as the narrative asks. Redrawn check plan (1:10,000, `redraw.py`, plan and checks unchanged): 237 massing footprints and the new street surfaces now show the grain inside the neighbourhoods; 7 landscape-link wedges sit where Hamlet, East and Woodside field reach open land beyond the site edge, while First, Second and Railway field and the cold-air field stop inside the site or meet the built garden city or rail, so they get none; the 31 labels are each placed once and none overlaps, 9 inside their feature along its long axis and 22 outside the strips on leader lines of 32 to 367 m, the longest ones (Chamer crossing, Railway field) still read poorly. The map margin grew from 60 to 320 m to make room for the labels. Largest gaps to the reference structure plan that remain: no translucent landscape around the site, no use colours inside the blocks, and fewer, shorter labels in the reference.

Draw the street and block grain inside the new neighbourhoods (local streets from streets/, footprints from massing/) instead of flat grey areas.
Place each label once, with a leader line where it would overlap another, and none across a strip edge ('Biotope row', 'Railway row', 'Underpass meadow' overlap now).
